title: Dataverse security roles: who can read or change which data?
summary: The page is held because the automation entry for cross-business-unit ownership names a tool and setting rather than a documented executable command. The permission model, licensing qualifications and other control operations are supported; a few navigation and checklist details also need tightening.

claims.claim: Dataverse security roles group privileges controlling access to tables and records in an environment.
claims.quote: Microsoft Dataverse uses a role-based security model to control access to a database and its resources in an environment.

claims.claim: The Dataverse security model applies only to environments with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: The model applies only to environments that have a Dataverse database.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: A role contains table privileges, miscellaneous task privileges and privacy-related privileges.
claims.quote: A security role consists of record-level privileges and task-based privileges of the following three types:

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Table privileges include Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, Append To, Assign and Share.
claims.quote: Table privileges define which tasks a user with access to a table record can do, such as Read, Create, Delete, Write, Assign, Share, Append, and Append To.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Privacy-related privileges include exporting data to Excel.
claims.quote: These privileges give a user permission to perform tasks that involve data that's integrated, downloaded, or exported outside of Dataverse, such as exporting data to Microsoft Excel or printing.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Access levels determine a privilege's reach through the business unit hierarchy.
claims.quote: Access levels determine how deep in the business unit hierarchy the user can perform the privilege.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: The access levels are Organization, Parent: Child Business Unit, Business Unit, User and None.
claims.quote: For organization-owned tables, miscellaneous privileges and privacy-related privileges only have access levels of Organization or None.
claims.fix: After the list, add: 'For organization-owned tables, miscellaneous privileges and privacy-related privileges, the available levels are only Organization or None.'

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Roles can be assigned directly to users or to Dataverse teams.
claims.quote: Assign security roles directly to users or to Dataverse teams.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Team members receive the team's privileges.
claims.quote: Team members receive the privileges assigned to the team.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; Risks and limits: Cumulative access
claims.claim: Users can have several roles and effective privileges are cumulative across roles and team memberships.
claims.quote: Security privileges are cumulative. A user receives the broadest access granted by all their roles and team memberships.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Business units define security boundaries.
claims.quote: Business units work with security roles to determine a user's access. They define security boundaries that help you manage users and data.

claims.where: What it is; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Roles are associated with business units.
claims.quote: Security roles are associated with business units.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Every user in an environment belongs to a business unit.
claims.quote: Every user in an environment belongs to a business unit.

claims.where: What it is: Roles that are not Dataverse roles
claims.claim: Tenant admin roles such as Power Platform administrator are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Tenant-level admin roles such as Power Platform administrator and Dynamics 365 administrator are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Tenant admin is not data access
claims.claim: Tenant admin roles do not automatically grant Dataverse data access.
claims.quote: However, these roles don't automatically grant Dataverse data access.

claims.where: What it is: Roles that are not Dataverse roles
claims.claim: Environments without Dataverse use Environment Admin and Environment Maker as their predefined environment roles.
claims.quote: Environment Maker and Environment Admin are the only predefined roles for environments that have no Dataverse database.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Sharing is the exception
claims.claim: Microsoft advises record sharing only for exceptions because it is less efficient and harder to troubleshoot.
claims.quote: Use sharing only for exceptions because it performs less efficiently and can be harder to troubleshoot than role-based access.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Roles do not unlock columns
claims.claim: Column-level security is configured separately and needs existing record access plus a column security profile.
claims.quote: Column-level security doesn't grant access to a record. A user must already have record access before a column security profile can grant access to secured columns.

claims.claim: Filtered record ownership grants access using column-value filters.
claims.quote: Filtered record ownership lets admins control access to Dataverse records with column-value filters.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Filtered record ownership is preview
claims.claim: Filtered record ownership is a preview feature.
claims.quote: Filtered table record ownership (preview)

claims.claim: Basic User and Environment Maker are automatically assigned to all users added to Dataverse in the Default environment type.
claims.quote: For the Default environment type, Basic User and Environment Maker roles are assigned automatically to all users added in Dataverse.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Environment Maker for Copilot Studio authors or another predefined or custom role for different permissions.
claims.quote: Assign the Environment Maker role to users who need to author agents. If the user needs a different set of permissions, assign another predefined role or a custom role.

claims.claim: Tenant admins no longer receive Dataverse System Administrator automatically.
claims.quote: Previously, Microsoft Entra ID admins, including Power Platform admins and Dynamics 365 service admins, were automatically assigned the System Administrator role in Dataverse. This is no longer the case.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Tenant admin is not data access
claims.claim: Removing an admin's tenant service-admin role does not automatically remove an existing Dataverse System Administrator assignment.
claims.quote: removing them from the Power Platform admin and Dynamics 365 service admin roles will not automatically remove their System Administrator role in Dataverse.

claims.claim: The security-role documentation publishes no separate role-specific price, licence or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse security roles separate price license meter security roles pricing PowerShell assign role; read database-security, security-roles-privileges, assign-security-roles, wp-security-cds and pricing-billing-skus on Microsoft Learn; no role-specific charge stated.

claims.claim: Presence in an environment does not grant data access; users still need an appropriate security role and required product licence.
claims.quote: A user's presence in an environment doesn't grant access to Dataverse data. The user must still have an appropriate security role and any required product license.

claims.claim: Dataverse tracks access separately for each database.
claims.quote: Dataverse tracks access separately for each database

claims.claim: Users need an appropriate Dataverse licence.
claims.quote: the user must have an appropriate Dataverse license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Where licence-to-role mappings are defined, valid licensed users automatically receive mapped roles.
claims.quote: If defined in your environment, certain roles are automatically assigned to users when users are added to Dataverse based on the license the users are assigned.

claims.claim: Removing the corresponding licence automatically removes its mapped role.
claims.quote: Removal of the respective license results in automatic role removal.

claims.claim: Licence-based default role management does not apply to Dataverse for Teams, Trial or Developer environments.
claims.quote: License-based default role management isn't applicable for users in these types of environments: Dataverse for Teams, Trial, and Developer.

claims.claim: An application user can be created without a licence.
claims.quote: You can create an unlicensed application user in your environment.

claims.claim: Dataverse auditing can record changes to security roles.
claims.quote: Changes to security roles.

claims.claim: Dataverse audit logs consume log storage capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.claim: A second role cannot hide a record exposed by another role.
claims.quote: if one role grants organization-level read access to all contact records, another role can't hide a specific contact from the user.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Tenant admin is not data access
claims.claim: A tenant admin needs the System Administrator Dataverse role in the particular environment to work with its data.
claims.quote: To work with data in a Dataverse environment, a tenant admin must also be assigned the System Administrator Dataverse security role in that specific environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Everyone needs a role
claims.claim: Every user needs at least one role, directly or through a group team, for service access.
claims.quote: You must assign at least one security role to every user either directly or indirectly as a member of a group team. The service doesn't allow access to users who don't have at least one security role.

claims.claim: An assigner cannot assign a security role with more privileges than the assigner holds.
claims.quote: the person who is assigning the security role can't assign someone else to a security role that has more privileges than the assigner.

claims.claim: Delegating role assignment to a non-System Administrator requires a suitably privileged custom role.
claims.quote: Assign Dataverse security roles | System Administrator security role, or a custom Dataverse role with at least Read and Assign privileges on the Security Role table

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The predefined-role reference says its listed Dataverse predefined roles cannot be edited.
claims.quote: The following list provides the predefined security roles in an environment that has a Dataverse database. You can't edit these roles.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited; controls[0].note
claims.claim: The editing guide documents editing privileges but excludes System Administrator and advises copying it.
claims.quote: You can't edit the System Administrator security role. Instead, copy the System Administrator security role and make changes to the new role.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited
claims.claim: Some predefined roles cannot be copied; Microsoft suggests creating a custom role instead.
claims.quote: Some predefined roles can't be copied. Try creating a custom security role instead.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Predefined roles cannot be edited
claims.claim: The assignment guide states that custom security roles are not supported for canvas apps.
claims.quote: It's important to note that custom security roles are not supported for canvas apps.

claims.claim: Organization access reaches records across all business units.
claims.quote: Users can access all records in the organization, regardless of the business unit hierarchical level they or the environment belong to.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Moving between environments
claims.claim: Solutions can move security roles between environments.
claims.quote: Use Dataverse solutions to move security roles and column security profiles between environments.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Moving between environments
claims.claim: Business units, teams and user assignments must be managed separately in each environment.
claims.quote: Create and manage business units and teams separately in each environment. You must also assign users to the appropriate security components in each environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Filtered record ownership is preview
claims.claim: Microsoft says preview features are not intended for production.
claims.quote: Preview features aren't meant for production use and may have restricted functionality.

claims.where: Risks and limits: PowerShell gap; Open questions
claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentRoleAssignment applies to environments without Dataverse and returns 403 for one with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: Sets permissions to an environment without a Dataverse database. If you make this call to an environment with a Dataverse database instance, you receive a 403 Forbidden error.

claims.claim: Role privileges can be edited through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + Permissions > Security roles > security role.
claims.quote:
Expand Users + permissions and select Security roles.
6. Choose the security role you want to edit.
7. Specify privileges for the security role.

claims.claim: POST to the v9.2 role-bound Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole action adds role privileges.
claims.quote: POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/roles(44ee44ee-ff55-aa66-bb77-88cc88cc88cc)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: User role assignments are managed through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote:
Select Users + permissions, and then select Users.
6. On the Users page select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.claim: POST to the v9.0 systemuserroles_association/$ref endpoint assigns a role to the identified user with the role's @odata.id.
claims.quote: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: Who can change roles
claims.claim: Assigning roles requires System Administrator or a custom role with at least Read and Assign on Security Role.
claims.quote: System Administrator security role, or a custom Dataverse role with at least Read and Assign privileges on the Security Role table

claims.claim: The role overview's troubleshooting table instead lists System Administrator or a tenant-level admin role.
claims.quote: Only users with the System Administrator role or a tenant-level admin role can manage security role assignments.

claims.claim: The path through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user opens application-user role selection.
claims.quote: Select + New app user to open the Create a new app user pane.
claims.fix: Extend the UI path to 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user > Create a new app user > edit icon (security roles)'. The existing note already explains choosing the target application and business unit; the omitted final icon is the role-selection control.

claims.claim: pac admin assign-user supports --environment, an application ID in --user, --role and the --application-user switch.
claims.quote: Object ID or user principal name (UPN) of Microsoft Entra ID user to be assigned to the environment or Application ID if assigning an Application User.

claims.claim: An environment permits one application user per Entra application registration.
claims.quote: In an environment, you can only have one application user for each Microsoft Entra–registered application.

claims.claim: Licence mappings can be viewed through Environments > environment > Settings > Users + Permissions > License To Role mapping.
claims.quote: Go to Environments > [select an environment] > Settings > Users + Permissions > License To Role mapping.

claims.claim: No API or command for License To Role mapping was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "License To Role mapping" API PowerShell Dataverse; Dataverse "license" "mapping" "table" API; "LicenseToRoleMapping" Dataverse API; "License To Role mapping" "API". Read assign-security-roles and pac admin; no mapping operation found.

claims.claim: Record ownership across business units is under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features.
claims.quote:
Select Settings > Product > Features.
5. Turn on Record ownership across business units.

claims.claim: 'OrgDBOrgSettings tool: change the EnableOwnershipAcrossBusinessUnits setting' is an automation call for the control.
claims.quote: Searched: OrgDBOrgSettingsTool.exe Update EnableOwnershipAcrossBusinessUnits command syntax. Read wp-security-cds and support.microsoft.com/help/2691237: they document the setting and executable Update syntax, not the printed prose as a call.
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'Microsoft.Crm.SE.OrgDBOrgSettingsTool.exe Update /u <organization-unique-name> EnableOwnershipAcrossBusinessUnits <value>' and set its docs URL to https://support.microsoft.com/help/2691237/orgdborgsettings-tool-for-microsoft-dynamics-crm. Add to the note: 'EnableOwnershipAcrossBusinessUnits stores the feature state, as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/wp-security-cds.' The support page gives 'Update [/u] <OrgName> <SettingName> <Value>'; retain a value placeholder rather than inventing a value format.

claims.claim: The documented UI procedure requires a Dynamics 365 admin or Power Platform admin.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Power Platform admin center as a Dynamics 365 admin or Microsoft Power Platform admin.

claims.claim: EnableOwnershipAcrossBusinessUnits stores the feature state and can be changed with OrgDBOrgSettings.
claims.quote: The EnableOwnershipAcrossBusinessUnits setting stores the state of this feature. You can also change the setting with the OrgDBOrgSettings tool for Microsoft Dynamics CRM.

claims.claim: Security Role auditing is under Environments > environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Entity and field audit settings > Entities > Security Role > General > Data Services > Auditing.
claims.quote:
In the left side panel, under Entities, select Security Role.
4. On the General tab, under Data Services, select Auditing.

claims.claim: PUT to v9.2 EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='role') updates the Security Role table definition.
claims.quote: PUT [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='new_bankaccount') HTTP/1.1
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/reference/entities/role to sources: its Properties table identifies Security Role's LogicalName as 'role', substantiating the target used with the cited generic table-definition update operation.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: The security-role Audit report is under Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > Audit report.
claims.quote:
Select Environments > [select an environment] > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles.
3. Select Audit report in the command bar.
claims.fix: Replace the prose path with 'Power Platform admin center > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > Audit report' so the route includes the environment-selection context.

claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review the Audit report and confirm self-elevation, but neither operation has its own control row.
claims.quote: Turn on auditing for the Security Role table and read the Audit report for recent role changes. / Confirm which admins have self-elevated, and who may assign roles.
claims.fix: In What to check, narrow the audit bullet to 'Turn on auditing for the Security Role table.' Narrow the final bullet to 'Confirm who may assign roles.' The existing table covers enabling table auditing and assigning roles, not opening the report or reviewing self-elevation.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Role assignment and removal are audit events 53, 54, 55 and 56 for teams and users.
claims.quote:
53 | Assign Role To Team | Associate
54 | Remove Role From Team | Disassociate
55 | Assign Role To User | Associate
56 | Remove Role From User | Disassociate

claims.where: Governance controls: Who can change roles
claims.claim: Power Platform, Dynamics 365 and Global Administrators must self-elevate before assigning Dataverse roles.
claims.quote: Power Platform, Dynamics 365, and Global Administrators are no longer automatically assigned the Dataverse System Administrator role. They must self-elevate before assigning Dataverse roles.

claims.where: Governance controls: Who can change roles
claims.claim: A Dynamics 365 Administrator must belong to the environment's security group.
claims.quote: A Dynamics 365 Administrator must belong to the environment's security group. This restriction doesn't apply to Global Administrators or Power Platform Administrators.

claims.where: controls[4].governs; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Enabling Record ownership across business units permits assigning roles from different business units regardless of the user's business unit.
claims.quote: When the allow record ownership across business units is enabled, you can assign security roles from different business units to your users irrespective of which business unit the users belong to.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Environment auditing must be enabled before auditing security roles.
claims.quote:
Prerequisites
Turn on auditing in your environment.

claims.claim: The table definition's IsAuditEnabled.Value property controls whether the table supports auditing.
claims.quote: To change which tables and columns support auditing, update their IsAuditEnabled.Value property.

claims.claim: Audit configuration metadata changes require publishing table customizations to take effect.
claims.quote: Changes don't take effect until you publish the table customizations.

claims.claim: Updating a table definition requires preserving existing properties rather than sending only a changed property.
claims.quote: you must use the PUT method when updating data model entities and be careful to include all the existing properties that you don't intend to change. You can't update individual properties.

claims.where: Governance controls: What the controls do not enforce
claims.claim: Power Platform data policies let administrators control connector access.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin center data policies allow administrators to control access to these connectors in various ways to help reduce risk in your organization.

claims.where: Open questions: Power Platform admin PowerShell
claims.claim: A dedicated Power Platform admin PowerShell cmdlet for assigning Dataverse security roles remains undocumented in the research.
claims.quote: Searched: "Dataverse" "PowerShell" "assign" "security role" cmdlet. Read Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentRoleAssignment and pac admin references; found the non-Dataverse PowerShell command and a Dataverse CLI command, not a Power Platform admin PowerShell equivalent.

claims.claim: During application-user creation, the administrator chooses an application and business unit, then uses the edit icon to select security roles.
claims.quote:
Under Business Unit, select a business unit from the dropdown list.
Select the edit icon to select security roles for the new application user.

claims.claim: Application users can hold security roles governing their environment data access.
claims.quote: You can select or deselect roles, and then select Save. All selected roles become the current assigned roles for the application user. Any unselected roles aren't assigned.
